# Writing and Critically Appraising Sample Size Justifications {#sec-reporting-and-appraisal}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Learning objectives"}
- Write a reproducible sample-size methods paragraph.
- Critically appraise adequacy of reported assumptions.
:::

## The idea

A defensible sample-size statement reports the **primary endpoint, estimand, formula or algorithm, input estimates with sources, precision or type I error and power, group allocation, all relevant design adjustments, anticipated missingness, rounding and final required numbers**. When specialised designs are used, additional parameters are necessary. In trials, the current CONSORT 2025 explanation item 16a requires assumptions supporting sample size determination.

## When and how to apply it

The planned target should be specified prospectively. A convenient sample retrospectively labelled “calculated” is not equivalent to a pre-study justification. Protocol reports should identify the planned estimation or testing framework and the exact units of all clinically meaningful differences.

## Teaching case 1 — baseline draft

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Clinical scenario / initial worked example"}
Draft a paragraph for a prevalence estimate with $p=0.50$, $d=0.05$, 95% confidence and 10% anticipated non-response, explicitly naming the rounding approach.
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Common error"}
“Sample size was calculated using 95% confidence and 80% power” is insufficient, especially without endpoint, assumptions and anticipated effect.
:::

## Key message

A reproducible sample-size paragraph explains the question, method, inputs and adjustments.
